title: Path sparkline profiles and span probe interaction notes (draft)
content:
Purpose
Short brainstorming + lightweight wireframe notes for a more compact request-trace view that emphasizes per-path "sparklines" and quick-span probes. Goal: give engineers fast at-a-glance signal about where time/variance lives across an individual request and let them jump into a small inspector without leaving the waterfall context.

Background
Current waterfall in Console is great for deep investigations but is visually heavy and forces tunnel-mode when users want quick triage. Many support/SE workflows want to: scan a request, see repeated hotspots across recent samples, and pop an inline inspector for a span to check headers/logs/kvs without opening a full trace detail panel.

High-level idea
1) Path sparkline profile: a thin row above the waterfall showing a compact, sampled timeline for the request path. Each sparkline is generated per-path (group by route + inferred downstream services) and shows median/95th percentiles across recent N samples. Clicking a sparkline filters the waterfall to that path.

2) Span probe micro-inspector: hover or click on a span to open a small, detachable probe card anchored to that span. Probe card contains: span summary (name, type, duration, error flag), 1–2 recent logs, top related tags, and quick actions (re-run sample, copy trace-id, open full inspector). Should be keyboard accessible (Enter to pin, Esc to close).

3) Compact mode: switch waterfall into a compressed layout (no vertical margins, minimized timestamps) where span rows compress into short 'span chips' but still show colored latency bars. Compact mode is ideal for tables/list of traces where density matters.

Wireframe notes (visual primitives)
- Top-of-trace header: path-sparkline-bar with a small legend (median / 95p). Each sample point rendered as a tiny vertical hairline; shading behind indicates variance. On hover show small tooltip with exact stats and sample time.
- Waterfall: each span row keeps left axis (service.name / operation) and right aligned duration marker. Latency bars become semi-transparent to avoid visual clutter.
- Span chip: rectangle with left color stripe (status), central microbar (relative duration), and suffix with 1–2 icon affordances (logs, tags). Clicking the chip invokes the span probe.
- Probe card: 320x220px default, anchored to span chip. Contains header (span name + duration + chevron to open full-view), body (2–3 lines of logs or key tag-value pairs), footer (actions: copy, open, mute, create-incident). Probe can be dragged; pin keeps it persistent as user scrolls.

Interaction flows
- Flow A (triage): user opens a trace list, toggles compact mode, scans path sparklines for abnormal spike, clicks sparkline -> waterfall filtered to that path -> clicks a red span chip -> probe opens showing 2 recent logs -> user copies trace-id and files an incident.
- Flow B (investigate variance): user in trace detail switches on 95p overlay for sparkline; toggles sample view to see individual sampled traces. They pin the probe on a suspicious span and scrub other samples using left/right arrow keys (probe updates logs/tags for each sample).

Design decisions and rationale
- Sparklines vs. heatmap: sparklines are lightweight, easier to interpret for a single request path, and map directly to path-level groupings. Heatmap is better for cluster-level overviews — keep for future.
- Probe size constrained to avoid occluding waterfall; detach/pin option for deeper dives.
- Keep click target large for span chips (48px min) to improve usability in dense views.
- Keyboard-first controls for accessibility and power users: navigable spans, probe pin/unpin, sample scrub via arrows.

Backlog / implementation slices (MVP -> later)
- MVP (slice 1): implement span chip and probe card with minimal data (span name, duration, 1 log line). Keyboard open/close. Basic sparkline rendering for a single request using last 10 samples. (JIRA: TRACE-UX-2101)
- Slice 2: path-level grouping for sparklines, 95p overlay, tooltip stats. Add copy & open full actions. (JIRA: TRACE-UX-2102)
- Slice 3: pinned probes across samples, sample scrub keyboard, small drag/dock UX. Integrate with full trace inspector. (TRACE-UX-2103)
- Later: path variance heatmap, auto-suggested spans to probe (anomaly detection), persisted user probes in notebook view.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Samples retention: how many historical samples do we fetch for sparklines by default? (10 vs 50) Cost/latency tradeoffs for fetching logs for probe per-sample.
- Backend endpoints: need an endpoint that returns a compact path profile (median, p95, sample timestamps) without full trace payload. Suggest: /v1/observability/paths/{path}/profile?limit=20
- Security: probe exposing logs/headers might surface PII. Need role-based gating and redact-by default. Work with security team on policy.

Edge cases and accessibility
- Long span names should truncate with ellipsis; tooltip reveals full name.
- Small viewports: probe should reflow into a full-width bottom drawer on mobile.
- Colorblindness: use patterned fills or distinct hatching for error/ok overlays where needed.

Notes to engineers / next steps
- Engineering pairing session requested: 2024-11-14 with Ethan and Ravi to prototype span chip CSS and probe anchor behavior.
- UX: quick mock in Figma with three states: default, compact, probe-pinned. Try to reuse existing timeline color tokens. (Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/trace-ux-proto)
- Product: prioritize MVP 1 for Q1 sprint. Decide sampling defaults and telemetry events for probe usage (open, pin, copy).

Open action items
- Aisha: draft API contract for path profile endpoint and share with backend by 2024-11-10.
- Ravi: spin up a lightweight React sandbox for probe anchor behavior by 2024-11-18.
- Sofia: create Figma mock and handoff tokens by 2024-11-12.

Quick links / references
- Existing waterfall code: GH:repo/console/src/components/waterfall (see existing span row and tooltip code)
- Incident workflow notes: confluence/OBS-incident-response

Rough prioritization (one-liner)
- Very high: span probe MVP (fast triage wins for CS + SE)
- High: path sparkline basic profile
- Medium: pinned probes and sample scrub
- Low: full heatmap and anomaly-suggested spans

Unresolved design tidbits (for next sync)
- Should probe show raw headers or just key redacted summary? (security input required)
- Where does the pinned probe state persist (per-user local vs server-side)?
- Exact sparklines color mapping when multiple downstream services exist on a single path.

End notes
This is intentionally a working-doc. The aim is to capture an alternative lightweight interaction model for quick trace triage that leads with per-path sparklines and small, contextual probes anchored to spans. Feedback welcome — add comments or ping in #console-design.
